title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) changes deterministic-invariant acceptance relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we executed 200 preregistered tasks with hosted model gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Provider-call accounting records 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair (201 model calls total). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 yield paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 (exact-binomial tail convention for n = 1,k = 1); paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step required_sequence ordering violation in an extreme-difficulty task (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3). We report the preregistration, deterministic reconciliation, full execution accounting (start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00, elapsed ≈29 min), paired analysis, representative diagnostics for the repaired pair, and limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Translating high-level operator intent into device-level configuration remains a central NetOps challenge. Proposed LLM-driven intent→configuration pipelines must satisfy deterministic invariants relevant to operational correctness: ordering/sequence constraints, group-level availability constraints, permitted field edits, and syntactic/semantic device-template constraints. A practical guarded pipeline couples generation to a verifier that can accept or reject a candidate and, when permitted, request a bounded repair. Prior prototype systems and benchmarks illustrate feasibility of generator→validator architectures, but they leave open how much marginal benefit bounded verifier-triggered repair provides when the exact same initial generated candidate is reused for both baseline and guarded comparisons.

We designed a preregistered paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) to isolate the marginal effect of a single verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under this design the identical sampled initial candidate is deterministically reused by both the baseline and guarded episodes; therefore any paired difference can only arise from the deterministic verifier and the single permitted automated repair. This narrow estimand addresses the specific empirical question: does a verifier-triggered bounded repair change per-task acceptance when starting from the same initial generation? We emphasize that this estimand does not measure effects from independent guarded first-pass generations, prompt conditioning, or multi-candidate selection.
sections.related_work:
Work on intent→configuration pipelines and LLM-augmented NetOps has advanced prototype systems and benchmark-style evaluations [1, 39, 40, 41]. Deterministic configuration verification methods provide operational oracles that can encode ordering, reachability, and group constraints appropriate for evaluating generated configurations [2, 76]. In software engineering and program-repair domains, generate→validate→repair loops have been demonstrated to improve artifact correctness in domain-specific settings (e.g., test-in-the-loop program repair), motivating analogous guarded pipelines in NetOps [52]. Tool-augmented agent designs and controlled integrations of LLMs with solvers or validators further show architectural promise but underscore engineering and evaluation challenges when applying these patterns to multi-device network workflows [23, 66].

Synthesis and gap. The supplied literature establishes (i) active prototyping and benchmarking of intent→config workflows, (ii) utility of deterministic verifiers as evaluation oracles, and (iii) promise of generate→validate→repair patterns in adjacent domains. However, the supplied records do not provide controlled, paired experiments that measure the repair-only marginal effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics in a deterministic verifier-backed NetOps task bank. Our experiment fills this narrow, reproducible gap by measuring exactly that repair-only estimand with full archived artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and fixed prior to model calls. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the per-task difference in the binary outcome 'all specified deterministic invariants pass' when comparing the guarded condition (generate→validate→≤1 repair) to baseline (single-shot initial candidate), paired per task. The preregistration fixed N = 200 tasks, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exact one sampled initial generation reused by both episodes), a maximum of one automated repair per task, primary failed-call treatment complete_pair_primary, and the confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar via exact binomial tail) plus a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Task generator and deterministic verifier. Tasks were produced by a deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 per a fixed index rule; each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated commands, enforces allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, checks required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), and returns full_intent_constraint_validation only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. The verifier emits structured tracer outputs that are authoritative for per-episode scoring and are archived.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and model configuration. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: the exact same single sampled candidate per task was deterministically provided to baseline and guarded episodes; hence any paired difference can only arise from deterministic validation and the single permitted repair. The model-configuration record declares the requested model as gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null/unset. We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a possible background property even though the experiment used one initial sample per pair by design.

Sanitizer, repair policy, and provider accounting. Before verifier parsing a deterministic formatting sanitizer ran. If the verifier reported invariant violations, the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model with a repair prompt constructed from the verifier trace (preregistered). Repair calls were counted against maximum_model_calls. Deterministic reconciliation records shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1, summing to hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; cache_miss_count = 201 and cache_hit_count = 0 indicate fresh provider generations for all calls.

Statistical procedures and exact tests. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar test computed from discordant pair counts n10 and n01 using the exact-binomial-tail convention implemented in the analysis executor. For our observed discordance (n = n10 + n01 = 1, k = n10 = 1) this yields p = 1.0. The paired absolute risk difference was estimated with a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) producing [0.00, 0.015]. All analysis parameters and seeds are recorded in archived analysis logs. Primary analysis followed complete_pair_primary; sensitivity treatments were preregistered for persistent unparsables (none observed).
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. The execution manifest records start 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and end 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (elapsed ≈29 minutes). planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}; cache_miss_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0.

Confirmatory outcomes. From archived analysis artifacts: baseline successes = 199, baseline failures = 1 (baseline success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200, guarded failures = 0 (guarded success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency: n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0050000000000000044. Exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial-tail convention; n = 1, k = 1) yields p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.00, 0.015]. These numeric artifacts reproduce when the archived analysis executor is re-run on the raw results.

Single repair diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Archived validator traces identify the repaired pair’s task as extreme difficulty with required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme". The verifier trace documents validation_before.violation_codes indicating the required_sequence ordering breach and validation_after.valid = true once the bounded repair was applied. The repair corrected the sequencing (reordering dependent commands) so the verifier accepted the configuration (score = 1, scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION"). The archived provider- and verifier-trace fields substantiate that the single observed paired improvement derived from the permitted repair applied to the shared initial candidate.

Representative diagnostics. Representative task manifests in the archive show required_command_count values spanning 3–9 and changed_interface_count up to 3; the lone baseline failure is associated with an extreme composite difficulty pattern consistent with the preregistered exploratory hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate residual failures. No persistent unparsables, no preregistered exclusions, and deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true were recorded.
sections.discussion:
What the paired estimand measured. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the experiment isolates the repair-only marginal effect: both baseline and guarded conditions begin with the identical sampled generation, and only deterministic validation plus the single permitted repair can produce a paired difference. The archived evidence supports a precise statement: when starting from the same initial candidate produced by gpt-5-mini in this synthetic task bank, a single permitted verifier-triggered repair converted one invalid ordering sequence into a verifier-acceptable configuration.

Statistical regime, ceiling effects, and power. The preregistered power rationale targeted detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 percentage points) at N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (baseline ~45–65%). The observed baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) produces a sparse-discordant regime: only one discordant pair (n = 1) yields limited directional evidence in the exact McNemar test (p = 1.0) while the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] bounds plausible absolute improvements by repair under this repair-only estimand. Practically, unexpectedly high baseline performance reduces realized inferential sensitivity for detecting small repair-only effects; the bootstrap interval quantifies that limitation and provides an upper bound (1.5 percentage points) compatible with our data and design.

Failure-mode analysis and implications for repair design. The single repaired failure was an ordering (required_sequence) violation spanning three interfaces and nine required commands; the available bounded repair prompt—constructed from the verifier trace—elicited a reorder that satisfied the verifier’s sequencing constraints. This concrete diagnostic supports a narrowly scoped architectural implication: verifier-guided bounded repair can be effective for certain localized ordering/dependency violations that are fully expressible in the verifier’s encoded invariants. It does not establish that bounded repair will rectify omissions detectable only via dataplane emulation, nor that it will address complex cascading misconfigurations beyond the expressivity of the verifier’s manifest.

Threats to validity and external generality. Internal: shared_initial_candidate design intentionally isolates repair effects but does not capture sampling variability, prompt sensitivity, or independent guarded-first-pass effects. Construct: the deterministic verifier enforces task-manifest invariants but is not a substitute for live-device or dataplane emulation; some functional faults may be invisible to the verifier. External: single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank limit cross-model and production generality; adversarial contamination and multi-model variance were not evaluated. Conclusion: the evidence supports a narrowly bounded operational claim aligned with the preregistered estimand; broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, live emulation, adversarial contamination testing).

Concrete future validation questions. The archived run and artifacts enable specific follow-ups that remain within the original methodological space: (1) repeat the paired, shared_initial_candidate design across alternative hosted models to measure model-dependence of repair-success concentration; (2) switch generation_semantics to independent guarded-first-pass samples to measure selection/constraint effects; (3) extend verifier specifications to include dataplane-derived checks in an emulation loop to evaluate fixes that require runtime observation; and (4) stratify sampling to oversample extreme composite-difficulty tasks to increase power for repair-only effects concentrated in hard workflows. Each of these is a distinct experiment and was not executed in the present run.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected an ordering violation in an extreme task. Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports the constrained conclusion that verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults expressible by the verifier in this synthetic setting. Extending these findings to production deployments and broader operational questions requires additional, targeted experiments that go beyond the preregistered design and archived execution artifacts reported here.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
